summary: Possible credential-spray triggered account lockouts across multiple internal users
description: Multiple internal accounts experienced high volumes of failed SSO logins followed by several successful logins and eventual account lockouts. Initial detection came from our identity provider (Okta) anomalous sign-on alert rule. This ticket tracks triage, containment, and investigation steps for suspected credential-spray or harvested-credential reuse potentially originating from an external phishing campaign.
timeline: 2026-03-10 03:42 UTC - Okta anomalous sign-on alert triggered: > 150 failed attempts across 12 unique usernames in 30 minutes
2026-03-10 03:45 UTC - Automated account lockouts applied for 9 accounts per policy
2026-03-10 04:00 UTC - Two accounts showed successful sign-ins from unfamiliar IPs and new device fingerprints
2026-03-10 04:12 UTC - SRE/On-call notified via #security-alerts Slack; session revocation and emergency MFA challenges initiated
2026-03-10 05:08 UTC - Customers: none (internal-only incident). Legal and Security leadership paged; incident declared internal-security-investigation
detection_logs: Okta syslog snippet: event=failed_signon count=18 username=ajenkins ip=45.132.19.8 user_agent=Mozilla/5.0
Okta syslog snippet: event=successful_signon username=mkhan ip=203.0.113.49 device=Windows-Edge-105.0
AWS CloudTrail: ConsoleLogin Failed for 3 attempts from 45.132.19.8 against role/redwood-internal
VPN logs: no correlated access from those IPs within same window
Auth service (internal): refresh_token use from revoked session id=... blocked by revocation check
investigation_notes: Geo-IP for attacker IPs show distributed proxies: RU/UA/CDN/Tor exit nodes; multiple IPs clustered to two ASN ranges
User agent strings are generic and change across attempts; no single exploited SSO integration detected
SAML assertions inspected; no forged assertions seen — attacker appears to be using valid credentials rather than SAML replay
Cross-check with phishing reports: #sec-phish channel contains a user-reported suspicious email to several employees received 2026-03-09 21:10 UTC with a credential prompt link
Okta risk score was elevated for the successful sign-ins; MFA prompt was validated but users completed MFA — possible MFA fatigue or coercion, or legitimate MFA prompts following credential reuse
Preliminary hypothesis: large-scale credential stuffing using harvested credentials from external breaches or targeted phishing; not an Okta configuration compromise
No evidence yet of lateral access to production clusters or secrets exfiltration; IAM keys rotation not triggered automatically
comments: Marcus Liu (2026-03-10 04:05 UTC): Initial alert forwarded to Security Ops. Blocking rules in WAF are not expected to help SSO endpoint. Starting session revocation for affected users.
Samira Khan (2026-03-10 04:18 UTC): Forcing password reset and revoking active sessions for 9 locked accounts. Requesting SRE to list recent token grants and check token-cache TTLs for anomalies.

Evan Brooks - SRE (2026-03-10 05:22 UTC): Confirmed no anomalous API spikes in serving-runtime; IAM console attempts limited to service accounts flagged. Will run a quick audit of AWS CloudTrail for cross-account access.
Priya Shah - Legal (2026-03-10 05:45 UTC): No customer data involved per initial review. Keep Legal looped if any evidence of exfiltration or regulatory scope changes.
resolution: Containment in progress: affected accounts forced password reset, all active sessions revoked, suspicious IPs blocked at edge where feasible, password policy and MFA prompts reinforced via mandatory reset. Incident remains open pending root cause confirmation and full audit of privileged access.
next_steps: Complete forensics on CloudTrail and Okta logs for the full 72-hour window
Review phishing email artifacts and obtain hosted page captures for IOC extraction
Deploy additional rate-limiting on SSO endpoints and temporary stricter lockout thresholds
Rotate any service account keys that may have been used during the window and audit IAM role assumption logs
Draft internal notice summarizing recommended user actions (password reset, check device, report suspicious emails)
Schedule post-incident review and update runbooks with lessons learned
